records.title: [Efficacy-toxicity duality of Tripterygium wilfordii in treatment of rheumatic and immune diseases: mechanisms, strategies for toxicity attenuation and efficacy enhancement, and future perspectives].
records.abstract: Rheumatic and immune diseases constitute a major global disease burden. Tripterygium wilfordii demonstrates remarkable therapeutic efficacy in treating rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus and related conditions. However, its prominent hepatic, renal, and reproductive toxicities engender a characteristic "efficacy-toxicity duality", thereby limiting its broader clinical adoption and safe application. This study systematically synthesized domestic and international research over the past two decades to construct a regulatory network governing the "efficacy-toxicity duality" of T. wilfordii from an integrative "component-pathway-spatiotemporal-host(individual)" perspective. It dissected the underlying mechanisms linking efficacy and toxicity, elucidating that key constituents such as triptolide exert dual effects through intervention in shared signaling pathways, including nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2(Nrf2) and signal transducer and activator of transcription 3(STAT3), where the specific outcome of efficacy versus toxicity is dictated by defined "dose-time" windows, tissue distribution patterns, and individual host factors. The study further reviewed toxicity attenuation and efficacy enhancement strategies, including structural modification, targeted delivery, and combination pharmacotherapy. In response to three translational bottlenecks-inconsistent quality, inefficient delivery, and lagging evaluation-this work proposed the establishment of end-to-end quality control standards, the development of intelligent responsive delivery systems, and the integration of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence and organoids into an advanced "efficacy-toxicity" evaluation framework. Collectively, these efforts aim to provide an integrative theoretical framework and translatable innovation pathways for advancing T. wilfordii toward safe, controllable, and precision-oriented modern pharmaceuticals, thereby facilitating the modernization of traditional Chinese medicine and its global clinical dissemination.

records.title: Translational research models for variant subtype bladder cancers: A comprehensive review of the current landscape.
records.abstract: Bladder cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality in the United States, with most cases classified as conventional urothelial carcinoma. However, a substantial subset of patients presents with aggressive variant histologies, including sarcomatoid, plasmacytoid, and micropapillary subtypes. These variants are associated with early dissemination, treatment resistance, and limited evidence to guide subtype specific management. Despite their clinical relevance, progress in mechanistic understanding and therapeutic development has been hindered due to rarity, underrepresentation in clinical trials, and a research focus on conventional disease. A key impediment is the lack of translational model systems that maintain variant defining morphology, lineage programs, and tumor microenvironmental interactions. Recent advances in translational modeling technologies now provide new opportunities to interrogate the unique biology of variant subtype bladder cancers. In this review, we highlight key preclinical models commonly used in bladder cancer research, including patient-derived xenografts, humanized models, syngeneic systems, genetically engineered mouse models, organoids, and ex vivo explants, and highlight emerging applications in variant histologies. We also discuss innovative and integrative platforms, including hybrid experimental systems and computational approaches, that are beginning to overcome barriers imposed by tumor rarity and heterogeneity. Collectively, these evolving model systems will enable more faithful representation of variant subtype biology, tumor-microenvironment interactions, and therapeutic vulnerabilities, and provide a framework for developing subtype-specific, precision treatment strategies.

records.title: Lactate-associated pyruvate kinase muscle isoform 2 nuclear enrichment and ferroptotic stress responses in lung cancer.
records.abstract: Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death with therapeutic potential in cancer. However, metabolic alterations within the tumor microenvironment may influence the sensitivity of lung cancer cells to ferroptotic stress. This study investigated the association between lactate exposure, pyruvate kinase muscle isoform 2 signaling, and cellular responses to RSL3-induced ferroptotic stress. Human H1299 lung cancer cells were treated with lactate (20 mmol/L; 24 hours), RSL3 (2 μmol/L), and the pyruvate kinase muscle isoform 2-targeting compound shikonin (1 μmol/L). Pyruvate kinase muscle isoform 2 expression and subcellular localization were assessed by immunofluorescence, and pyruvate kinase muscle isoform 2 immunoreactivity was evaluated by immunohistochemistry. Patient-derived lung cancer organoids were used to assess 3-dimensional growth. Wound-healing and Transwell assays were performed to evaluate wound closure and Transwell cell counts, respectively. SLC7A11 and glutathione peroxidase 4 protein levels were examined by Western blotting. Under RSL3-induced ferroptotic stress, lactate treatment was associated with increased pyruvate kinase muscle isoform 2 nuclear enrichment and immunoreactivity, whereas shikonin partially attenuated these changes. Lactate partially alleviated RSL3-induced growth inhibition in patient-derived lung cancer organoids and increased wound closure and Transwell cell counts relative to RSL3 treatment alone. These lactate-associated phenotypic changes were partially attenuated by shikonin. RSL3 reduced SLC7A11 and glutathione peroxidase 4 protein levels, whereas lactate cotreatment increased the levels of both proteins. Shikonin attenuated the lactate-associated increase in glutathione peroxidase 4, while its effect on SLC7A11 was less pronounced. Lactate treatment was associated with increased pyruvate kinase muscle isoform 2 nuclear enrichment, higher SLC7A11 and glutathione peroxidase 4 protein levels, and partial attenuation of RSL3-induced growth inhibition. These findings suggest that lactate-associated pyruvate kinase muscle isoform 2 signaling may contribute to reduced sensitivity to ferroptotic stress in lung cancer. Further genetic and mechanistic studies are required to establish the causal role of pyruvate kinase muscle isoform 2 and determine whether nuclear pyruvate kinase muscle isoform 2 directly regulates SLC7A11 and glutathione peroxidase 4 expression.

records.title: Stage-specific exposure to an activity-permissive medium enhances neuronal activity in oligodendrocyte-enriched cortical organoids.
records.abstract: Oligodendrocyte-enriched cortical organoids (OCOs) are a powerful platform for modeling oligodendrogenesis in a human cellular context. However, neuronal activity is impaired in conventional culture media, limiting assessment of neuronal function in conjunction with oligodendrocyte biology. To address this, we used a modified BrainPhys medium termed neuronal activity medium (NAM) and defined the optimal developmental window for NAM exposure to generate OCOs with robust neuronal activity (NAM-OCOs). Stage-specific exposure to NAM, prior to oligodendrocyte expansion, leads to enhanced structural complexity, as evidenced by increased organoid size, heightened synaptogenesis, and upregulation of transcripts associated with neuronal morphology. Further, NAM-OCOs display increased cellular heterogeneity, with GABAergic interneurons exhibiting enhanced inhibitory synaptic features and a more advanced developmental transcriptional state, while preserving oligodendrocyte development and oligodendrocyte-axon associations. Altogether, our studies demonstrate that stage-specific exposure to an activity-permissive environment enhances neuronal activity, establishing an OCO model which integrates neuronal activity with oligodendrocyte development and differentiation.

records.title: Sinoatrial node dysfunction: molecular mechanisms, arrhythmogenesis, and translational pathways toward precision therapy.
records.abstract: Sinoatrial node dysfunction (SND) is a major cause of bradyarrhythmia, chronotropic incompetence, tachy-brady syndrome, and a common indication for permanent pacemaker implantation, particularly in older adults. Although SND has diverse etiologies, this review focuses on aging-associated intrinsic SND, while considering other common causes where they inform differential diagnosis, arrhythmogenic mechanisms, or therapeutic development. Although current medical interventions provide effective rhythm support, they does not correct the molecular and tissue-level processes that drive sinoatrial node (SAN) degeneration. The review integrates current knowledge of SAN biology with mechanisms underlying SND, including fibrosis, ion-channel and calcium-clock remodeling, mitochondrial dysfunction, cellular senescence, impaired β-adrenergic signaling, genetic susceptibility, and epigenetic or epitranscriptomic regulation. We further discuss how these mechanisms contribute to impaired impulse generation, SAN exit block, reduced chronotropic reserve, and increased susceptibility to atrial arrhythmia. We discuss approaches for studying the molecular and cellular mechanisms and evaluating therapeutic strategies using emerging animal models, human pluripotent stem cell-derived SAN-like pacemaker cells, organoids, assembloids, and single-cell and spatial omics platforms . Finally, we highlight translational opportunities, including senescence-directed, metabolic, antifibrotic, autonomic, gene-based, regenerative, and biological pacing strategies. A mechanism-guided classification of SND may support future precision therapies that complement conventional pacing by linking dominant rhythm phenotypes to targetable biological drivers, molecular and functional pharmacodynamic markers, and human-relevant models of pacemaker failure.

records.title: Patient-derived gastric cancer organoids for functional precision oncology: disease-specific bottlenecks and clinical readiness.
records.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) poses a distinct modeling challenge. The disease varies by region, histology, metastatic site, and treatment history. It also develops within a gastric niche shaped by acid, mucus, polarity, microbes, and stroma. Patient-derived organoids (PDOs) can preserve tumor-linked epithelial states and support living biobanks. They also enable genotype-phenotype studies and functional testing of therapeutic vulnerabilities. Their clinical value depends on representation, not model complexity alone. The assay must also return clear results within a useful clinical window. This review evaluates GC PDOs as functional companion models for precision oncology rather than stand-alone treatment decision tools. We discuss four barriers that limit clinical readiness. Establishment bias reduces representation of diffuse-type, scirrhous, and signet-ring cell carcinomas. Standard organoid lumens do not reproduce gastric acidity, stratified mucus, or Helicobacter pylori-driven polarity loss. Long-term expansion can select culture-adapted clones and weaken clinical representativeness. PDO drug screening also remains difficult to align with urgent treatment timelines. Fresh-sample assays may shorten turnaround time but reduce scale and depth. We further highlight biological insights gained from GC organoids. These include niche independence, epigenetic dependencies, ARID1A-linked vulnerabilities, and chemotherapy resistance. We propose a readiness framework based on six criteria: tumor authenticity, subtype coverage, niche fidelity, turnaround time, assay standards, and outcome validation. This framework may help define where GC PDOs can support clinical reasoning.

records.title: Dynamic Graph Prior-Guided Latent Adaptation for Generalizable Single-Cell Perturbation Response Prediction.
records.abstract: Predicting transcriptional responses to drug perturbations in unseen cellular contexts is a central challenge in single-cell perturbation modeling. This challenge creates a need for models that combine flexible state transitions with structured biological prior knowledge. Existing data-driven models often struggle to generalize across unseen cell types, while many prior-based models rely on static biological graphs without explicitly conditioning prior influence on perturbation-specific target support. We propose DGP-LA, a dynamic graph-prior latent adaptation framework that refines biological priors and injects them as gated latent corrections within a cell-state-conditioned transition model. DGP-LA couples a transition backbone with perturbation-conditioned sparse graph refinement. It propagates gene-aligned target support over the refined graph and selectively injects the resulting topology-aware signal into the hidden representation. On Tahoe and NeurIPS, DGP-LA improves Pearson Delta relative to State by 8.7% and 35.8% for generalization across unseen cell types. In zero-shot drug perturbation response prediction on unseen cell types, it improves Pearson Delta relative to CRISP by 79.1% and 67.6%. The model also improves DE-gene recovery, response discrimination, and Hallmark pathway recovery, supporting adaptive latent integration of biological priors for more generalizable and biologically interpretable perturbation modeling. DGP-LA's source code and reproducibility materials are available at https://github.com/bieyl/DGP-LA and archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22155398. Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

records.title: Benchmarking biological knowledge-graph priors against single-cell foundation models for Perturb-seq prediction.
records.abstract: Perturb-seq prediction increasingly relies on either biological graph priors or single-cell foundation models, but their relative value is difficult to interpret when architectures, split definitions and graph sources vary simultaneously. We benchmarked STRING functional associations and Gene Ontology co-annotation against dense, self-edge-only and exact-degree-rewired supports in one fixed graph-attention backbone, with a separate 200-HVG STRING-GO-control-co-expression sensitivity. Four public Perturb-seq datasets, three nested gene-space scales and three optimisation seeds were evaluated on held-out guide conditions; GEARS, scGPT and Geneformer were evaluated on the same held-out conditions, output-gene panels and Pearson-r metric after model-specific validity checks. At 200 highly variable genes, STRING-GO improved the equal-dataset Pearson r by +0.016 (95% interval [+0.010, +0.022]) relative to dense support. Dataset effects were positive in Adamson (+0.017), Norman (+0.015), Replogle K562 (+0.017) and Replogle RPE1 (+0.014), and 122/200 guide conditions improved (0.61 [0.54,0.68]). The top-20-gene Jaccard difference was +0.009 [+0.006,+0.012]. STRING-GO exceeded self-edge-only support by +0.024 [+0.018,+0.029] and the mean of ten exact-degree rewires by +0.011 [+0.005,+0.017]. The native-panel effect declined from +0.016 at 200 genes to +0.009 at 1000 genes; the 1000-200 interaction was -0.006 [-0.011,-0.002]. The primary graph-support comparison was formulated and conducted during peer-review revision rather than planned as an a priori confirmatory study. All three external models passed implementation-specific checks. Across 36 protocol-matched dataset-scale contrasts, 32 were within the descriptive ±0.030 reference envelope and four were outside, all favouring the external model. These results demonstrate a modest empirical predictive improvement under the evaluated matched protocol; they do not by themselves establish practical biological relevance.

records.title: AI-enabled fungal biomanufacturing: from genome mining to the artificial intelligence virtual cell.
records.abstract: Fungi are important chassis organisms for sustainable biomanufacturing owing to their strong secretion capacity, metabolic diversity, and adaptability to industrial processes. Driven by the rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), computational approaches that enable machines to learn patterns from data and make predictions, together with omics technologies and synthetic biology, data- and model-driven strategies are increasingly reshaping fungal cell factory design and optimization. This review summarizes recent advances in AI-enabled fungal biomanufacturing, covering AI-assisted genome mining, enzyme and pathway analysis, genome editing, metabolic network modeling, and intelligent fermentation control. The review further highlights the emerging concept of the artificial intelligence virtual cell (AIVC), which integrates multi-omics data, mechanistic modeling, and machine learning-based approaches into a unified multiscale framework for simulating dynamic cellular behaviors. The technical foundations and potential applications of AIVC in fungal metabolic engineering, drug discovery, agriculture, and environmental biotechnology are reviewed. Finally, key challenges-data quality and standardization, cross-scale model integration and interpretability, and the gap between in silico prediction and experimental validation-are highlighted. This review provides a systematic perspective on the role of AI and virtual cell technologies in advancing next generation fungal biotechnology.

records.title: PHAROS: turning single-cell perturbation models into target-directed drug-combination screens.
records.abstract: Combination therapies are central to cancer treatment, but exhaustive screening is impractical. We introduce PHAROS, a framework that turns a pretrained single-cell perturbation model into a target-directed search engine for drug combinations. PHAROS predicts how a cell population changes under a drug, one drug at a time, then chains these predictions together to simulate drug combinations. It scores each simulated outcome against the desired target state and uses a search algorithm to find the most promising combinations, all without retraining the underlying model. Across two independent combinatorial perturbation datasets, PHAROS recovered exact or mechanism-matched two-drug responses in cell lines, both seen and unseen during model training. Its rankings were specific to the requested conversion and were not explained by single-drug effects, additive effects, or shared mechanism of action. In exploratory analyses of patient-derived metastatic HR+/HER2- breast tumors and basal cell carcinoma (BCC), PHAROS prioritized FDA-approved regimens, distinguished combinations by their predicted tumor-versus-immune objective profiles, and nominated pathway-level hypotheses, while explicitly identifying both tumor cohorts as outside the model's supported distribution. PHAROS provides a modular route from pretrained virtual-cell models to inverse, single-cell combination-screening platforms.

records.title: Pop-Corn: Predicting Perturbation Phenotype Effects Across Single-Cell and Spatial Contexts.
records.abstract: Genetic perturbations can reshape cell populations by altering the relative abundance of specific cell types and states within the profiled population, including increases, decreases and states that become detectable after perturbation. Pooled single-cell screens, such as Perturb-seq, measure such responses at scale. However, only a small fraction of possible perturbations can be tested experimentally. A central challenge is therefore to predict compositional shifts induced by unseen perturbations. Many perturbation-prediction methods do not directly optimize for this outcome; instead, they predict gene-expression responses and infer cell-type and cell-state composition downstream. Surprisingly, we find that even models that accurately predict perturbation-induced changes in average gene expression perform poorly at forecasting these compositional shifts. To address this gap, we present Pop-Corn, a method that directly predicts how a perturbation reshapes cell-type composition without reconstructing gene expression. In the primary T-cell benchmark, Pop-Corn predicted the overall cell-state composition of held-out perturbations more accurately than the evaluated expression-prediction pipelines, while better preserving the diversity of observed cell states. We further extend Pop-Corn to intact tissue, where it predicts perturbation-induced cell-type proportion changes in local cellular neighborhoods and uses attention patterns to generate hypotheses about context-dependent cellular interactions. Retrospective virtual screens support the use of Pop-Corn to prioritize perturbations for experimental follow-up according to their predicted effects on cell-state composition.

records.title: Perspectives on tissue-selective insulin derivatives.
records.abstract: Insulin is a central regulator of metabolic homoeostasis with diverse, tissue-specific actions across multiple organs. Despite major advances in insulin formulations, current therapies rely on systemic delivery and do not reproduce the physiological distribution of endogenous insulin, resulting in non-physiological tissue exposure and associated metabolic limitations. In this perspective, we discuss emerging strategies aimed at achieving tissue-selective insulin action, including molecular engineering of insulin analogues, modulation of insulin receptor isoform specificity and targeted delivery approaches. Attention is given to hepato-preferential, muscle-directed, brain-targeted and adipose-modulating strategies, highlighting their mechanistic basis, therapeutic potential and inherent limitations. While proof of principle has been established for several approaches, challenges remain in balancing tissue selectivity with whole-body metabolic control. Advances in protein design and delivery technologies may ultimately enable the development of next-generation insulin therapies that better mimic physiological insulin action and improve clinical outcomes in metabolic and neurodegenerative diseases.

records.title: Coordinating structure-guided design and cis-regulatory optimization to engineer elite herbicide-tolerance alleles in crops.
records.abstract: Genome editing facilitates the rapid creation of elite alleles, yet identifying editable sites for durable trait improvement without functional trade-offs remains challenging. Most current strategies modify a single genetic axis, limiting their effectiveness and stability. Here we developed a dual-layer allele engineering framework integrating structure-guided protein design with precise cis-regulatory tuning to overcome such constraints. Using rice 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase (OsHPPD) as a model, structural analysis enabled the rational design of coding variants that retain enzymatic activity while conferring herbicide resistance. To further enhance resistance, we introduced a highly efficient 22-bp expression-modulating element into the engineered alleles, generating combinatorial coding and regulatory variants with significantly improved resistance, up to four times the recommended field application rate. Importantly, the dual-layer strategy was successfully applied in polyploid wheat, demonstrating its robustness and cross-species applicability. Our work establishes a versatile framework for functional allele engineering, offering a precise and broadly applicable route for crop improvement.

records.title: Discovery of an antagonist nanobody targeting the oxytocin receptor with tocolytic effect in mice.
records.abstract: Preterm birth, defined as delivery before 37 completed weeks of gestation, poses significant risks to maternal and neonatal health. These risks include neonatal respiratory distress syndrome, intraventricular hemorrhage, long-term developmental challenges, and in severe cases, mortality. Addressing these issues, G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR)-mediated tocolysis has become a focal strategy in pharmaceutical research to mitigate preterm labor risks. Most GPCR drugs are small molecules, yet their tendency to cross the placental barrier and induce fetal toxicity presents a significant challenge. Antibody drugs, with minimal cell membrane permeability, offer a promising alternative. In this study, we leverage AI-driven protein design to enable nanobody screening and identify several nanobodies with antagonist activity against the oxytocin receptor, a key target for preterm birth therapeutics. One of these nanobodies demonstrates antagonist activity comparable to Atosiban, a commonly used clinical drug, while exhibiting higher subtype selectivity. Pharmacological and structural analyses reveal mechanisms distinct from small molecule antagonists. These findings expand the pharmacological potential of antibody drugs and introduce useful tools and perspectives for developing effective tocolytic agents.

records.title: Integrated computation-guided thermostabilization of the fungal sweet protein Honey Truffle Sweetener.
records.abstract: Thermostability limits the use of sweet proteins as sugar substitutes in thermally processed foods. Here, we report an integrated computation-guided workflow for thermostabilizing Honey Truffle Sweetener (HTS), a recently identified fungal sweet protein with low intrinsic stability. We determined the HTS crystal structure and used it to guide subsequent computational analyses. Rosetta and ThermoMPNN evaluated candidate substitutions from complementary physics-based and deep-learning-based perspectives, and the selected single-mutant library was experimentally characterized. The resulting melting-temperature data were then used to develop SMRC-Net, which combines mutation-centered features from the ESM2 protein language model with molecular dynamics-derived structural descriptors to support mutation prioritization. Repeated nested cross-validation supported quantitative Tm prediction within the HTS scaffold, while prospective testing showed 9/10 directional agreement in a small, computationally selected variant set. Validated substitutions were then assembled stepwise in small modules, followed by the introduction of an engineered disulfide bond. The final variant, FM, had a melting temperature of 82.1 °C, 27.5 °C higher than that of wild-type HTS. Untreated FM retained sweetness, while separate heat- and pH-treatment assays showed retained solubility and largely preserved secondary-structure profiles. Sweetness after these treatments was not evaluated. Molecular dynamics analyses indicated that FM was not uniformly rigidified but instead exhibited localized flexibility redistribution and a more consolidated conformational ensemble. This work provides a practical computation-guided framework for protein thermostabilization, with potential applicability to other compact proteins.

records.title: Design-Evolution Synergy Enables New-to-Nature Enzyme Chemistry.
records.abstract: Directed evolution and machine-learning-assisted evolution have transformed biocatalysis by enabling rapid optimisation of catalytic performance within compatible protein scaffolds. In parallel, advances in deep-learning-driven de novo protein design have expanded accessible protein architectural space, enabling the generation of functional catalysts for increasingly challenging transformations. We herein report a synergistic design-evolution strategy to encode new-to-nature regio- and enantioselective C-H amination reactions using engineered de novo haemproteins to synthesise chiral piperidines, a privileged pharmacophore in drug discovery. By integrating motif scaffolding, computational re-design, and directed evolution, we demonstrate de novo enzyme design can enable challenging, high-energy-barrier enzyme chemistry with programmable regio- and enantioselectivity, high catalytic efficiency, excellent enzyme stability, and scaffold diversity.

records.title: RNASeek: A Cross-Phyla Generative Foundation Model for Multipurpose RNA Modeling and Reinforcement Learning-Based Design.
records.abstract: RNA plays central roles in regulating information flow and provides a versatile substrate for engineering biological functions. While large language models (LLMs) have transformed natural language processing and protein design, a general framework connecting RNA foundation models to functional sequence design remains limited. Here, we present RNASeek, a 1.6-billion-parameter generative foundation model built on a DeepSeek architecture and trained on a cross-phyla transcriptomic corpus for RNA sequence representation and generation. Natural-language tokens enable flexible conditional prediction and sequence design using a unified backbone. RNASeek captures species-specific transcript features and intron-exon boundaries in a zero-shot setting. We then fine-tune RNASeek to predict ribozyme self-cleavage activity and viral mRNA stability, revealing interpretable sequence features associated with function, including ribozyme loop flexibility and stem stability, as well as AU-rich motifs associated with mRNA stability. We use these functional predictors as reward models and apply Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to update RNASeek's generation policy toward sequences with desired properties. GRPO-guided generation produces faster-cleaving ribozymes and stability-enhancing 3' UTRs while satisfying user-specified IUPAC constraints. Experimentally validated RNASeek-generated ribozymes achieve wild-type levels of activity, while RNASeek-generated 3' UTR sequences exceed the performance of the training data and benchmarked AI-generated 3' UTRs. Together, RNASeek establishes a unified pretrain-predict-optimize framework that connects learned RNA function to controllable de novo sequence design and provides a general strategy for engineering regulatory RNAs with desired properties.

records.title: The use of TF-Ag-α to selectively capture tumor-derived extracellular vesicles and enhance the predictive performance of extracellular vesicle PD-L1 for response to immune checkpoint inhibitors.
records.abstract: Only a subset of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients benefits from immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Tissue PD-L1 has limited accuracy in predicting ICI response and requires invasive biopsies, highlighting the urgent need for reliable, minimally invasive biomarkers. Extracellular vesicle PD-L1 (EV PD-L1) is a promising liquid biopsy marker, but its predictive performance is confounded by PD-L1 derived from non-tumor cells. We developed a tumor-specific EVs-based assay to predict ICI response. Tumor-derived extracellular vesicles (TEXs) were selectively captured using the tumor-specific Thomsen-Friedenreich glycoantigen alpha (TF-Ag-α), and PD-L1 levels in TEXs expressing TF-Ag-α (i.e., TEXTF-Ag-α PD-L1) were measured in sera from 91 NSCLC patients receiving anti-PD-1 therapy (40 responders and 51 non-responders). Predictive performance was evaluated at pre-treatment baseline, at the end of first treatment cycle, and via fold changes. At pre-treatment baseline, TEXTF-Ag-α PD-L1 showed moderate predictive ability (AUC: 0.76; sensitivity: 0.97; specificity: 0.56). By the end of the first treatment cycle, responders exhibited a ~4.18-fold increase in TEXTF-Ag-α PD-L1 expression, whereas non-responders showed an approximate 20% decrease. Dynamic fold changes after the first treatment cycle substantially improved predictive performance, achieving an AUC of 0.93, sensitivity of 0.95, and specificity of 0.80 for distinguishing responders from non-responders, outperforming both total EV PD-L1 and tissue PD-L1. These results demonstrated that selective TEX capture using TF-Ag-α significantly enhanced the predictive value of EV PD-L1. Dynamic changes in TEXTF-Ag-α PD-L1 provided a highly accurate, minimally invasive biomarker for early assessment of anti-PD-1 response, supporting tumor-specific EVs-based liquid biopsy for precision immunotherapy.

records.title: Pediatric Liver Transplantation in the Treatment of Solid Liver Tumors: A Narrative Review.
records.abstract: Pediatric primary liver malignancies comprise a heterogeneous group of tumors requiring individualized multidisciplinary management. Hepatoblastoma and hepatocellular carcinoma remain the most common malignant liver tumors in children, whereas rare hepatic neoplasms account for a small but clinically significant proportion of cases. Over the past two decades, advances in tumor biology, standardized radiologic staging, multidisciplinary treatment planning, and liver transplantation have substantially improved outcomes, particularly for children with unresectable hepatoblastoma. Contemporary management has shifted from an anatomy-based approach to individualized treatment strategies that integrate molecular characterization, PRETEXT staging, response to neoadjuvant therapy, and careful assessment of surgical resectability. Liver transplantation is now recognized as a definitive oncologic treatment for carefully selected children with unresectable hepatoblastoma, selected cases of hepatocellular carcinoma, and, in exceptional circumstances, other rare hepatic malignancies. In parallel, improvements in post-transplant oncologic surveillance and immunosuppressive management have expanded opportunities for long-term disease control while emphasizing the need to balance graft preservation with recurrence risk. Emerging technologies, including molecular biomarkers, liquid biopsy, artificial intelligence, and advanced surgical planning, together with international collaborative initiatives, are expected to further refine patient selection and post-transplant management. This review summarizes current evidence on the role of liver transplantation in pediatric liver malignancies and discusses contemporary advances reshaping pediatric transplant oncology.

records.title: AI in Neuro-Oncology: An Overarching Review.
records.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across neuro-oncology domains to analyze complex, high-dimensional, multimodal data. Despite major advances in the biological understanding and classification of CNS tumors, clinical outcomes for many of them remain poor, reflecting intra- and inter-tumor heterogeneity and limitations of conventional reductionist approaches. AI offers a paradigm shift to capture this heterogeneity and provide quantitative, reproducible diagnostic, predictive, and prognostic insights. This article describes a joint effort across the Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology (RANO) working groups to provide an overarching review of the AI use across six key domains of neuro-oncology: neuroimaging, neuropathology, laboratory medicine, neurosurgery, drug discovery, and clinical trials. Applications closest to clinical use include imaging segmentation and quantification, AI-assisted image reconstruction, DNA methylation-based classification, and workflow optimization. Radiogenomics, WSI-based molecular prediction, AI-guided surgical targeting, liquid biopsy interpretation, AI-guided drug discovery, digital twins, and in silico trials remain promising but require stronger prospective validation. Key challenges include limited availability of large diverse datasets, variability in data acquisition and reference standards, and limited external validation. This review provides a unifying framework for understanding the role of AI across neuro-oncology and highlights key considerations for its responsible implementation, emphasizing standardization, reproducibility, multi-institutional validation, and human oversight.

records.title: Advances in Liquid Biopsy for Precision Oncology: Applications, Challenges, and Future Directions in Clinical Laboratories.
records.abstract: Liquid biopsy has emerged as a revolutionary, minimally invasive approach in precision oncology, enabling dynamic molecular profiling of tumors through analysis of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), circulating tumor cells (CTCs), exosomes, and other biomarkers in body fluids. Focusing specifically on recent advances from 2023 to 2026, this review provides a laboratory-centered critical synthesis addressing the core operational questions for clinical implementation: which liquid biopsy platform should be selected for specific analytes and clinical intents, under what pre-analytical and analytical constraints, and with what quality-control and clinical utility standards. Key technological developments include highly sensitive next-generation sequencing (NGS) with unique molecular identifiers (UMIs), digital droplet PCR (ddPCR), multi-omics integration, and artificial intelligence-assisted interpretation, which have improved detection sensitivity to ultra-low variant allele frequencies. Major clinical applications encompass multi-cancer early detection (MCED), companion diagnostics, real-time treatment monitoring, minimal residual disease (MRD) assessment, and resistance mutation tracking. These tools often provide earlier insights than imaging and better capture tumor heterogeneity. Compared with tissue biopsy, liquid biopsy offers advantages in repeatability, speed, and systemic representation, though challenges remain in sensitivity for early-stage disease, standardization, cost-effectiveness, and implementation in grassroots hospitals. Future directions emphasize multi-omics, AI, and automated workflows to enhance its role across the cancer continuum. This review highlights practical recommendations for clinical laboratories, positioning liquid biopsy as a cornerstone of personalized, proactive oncology care.

records.title: Precision surgical oncology for hepatocellular carcinoma.
records.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a heterogeneous tumor-liver-host disease in which treatment selection depends on tumor burden, liver function, portal hypertension, performance status, and patient preferences. Although hepatic resection and other established treatment modalities remain central to curative and disease-controlling strategies, emerging biological and digital technologies may provide additional information beyond conventional clinical assessment. However, their prognostic performance does not necessarily establish clinical utility, and many remain insufficiently validated for routine treatment selection. This narrative review examines the evolving role of precision-oriented approaches in HCC, including molecular and immune profiling, radiomics, circulating tumor DNA, artificial intelligence, and digital pathology. We classify these approaches into three evidence tiers: established clinical practice, investigational clinical tools, and future hypotheses. We then propose Precision Surgical Oncology as an author-developed, hypothesis-generating framework in which guideline-based assessment is followed by biological and host-risk refinement, multidisciplinary interpretation, individualized treatment within established therapeutic pathways, and longitudinal reassessment. Precision Surgical Oncology is intended to complement, rather than replace, evidence-based HCC management. Its future clinical value will depend on prospective validation, reproducibility, defined clinical actionability, equitable implementation, and demonstration of improved patient outcomes.

records.title: The epigenetic landscape of hepatocellular carcinoma: from molecular mechanisms to early detection biomarkers and precision therapy.
records.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of global cancer mortality due to late diagnosis, molecular heterogeneity, and therapeutic resistance. Emerging evidence highlights that epigenetic and epitranscriptomic dysregulations drive hepatocarcinogenesis by altering gene expression programs without changing the underlying DNA sequence. Aberrant DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin remodeling, non-coding RNA networks, and N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modifications collectively orchestrate HCC initiation, progression, metastasis, immune evasion, and metabolic reprogramming. Recent breakthroughs in next-generation sequencing, liquid biopsy, and multi-omics profiling have accelerated the identification of robust epigenetic biomarkers for early detection, prognosis, and therapeutic monitoring. Concurrently, epigenetic-targeted therapies, including DNA methyltransferase, histone deacetylase, EZH2, and BET inhibitors, offer promising preclinical and clinical opportunities for precision oncology, particularly through rational combination strategies to overcome drug resistance. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of the molecular mechanisms governing epigenetic and epitranscriptomic alterations in HCC. We highlight their translational potential in clinical practice and critically discuss current challenges, emerging technologies, and future perspectives for successful clinical implementation.
